Chapter 5: The Father’s Primacy—Honoring the Source of All Love.
When you step into a Catholic church, you find yourself surrounded by prayers and rituals that reach upward, drawing the whole community into something bigger than themselves. But have you ever noticed how, even though the prayers of the Mass are addressed to the Father, our attention often lingers on the Son or the Holy Spirit?
The Votive Mass of the Divine Heart of God the Father invites us to pause and remember the heart of it all—the unique role of the Father as the source and summit of every act of love. This isn’t just about getting theology right. It’s about a real, lived experience. Picture a quiet sanctuary, filled with a gentle awe, as people reflect on what it means for the Father to come first—not in authority alone, but as the wellspring of all creation. The readings at Mass gently remind everyone that everything—every act of mercy, every moment of grace—begins in the Father’s heart. Imagine a catechist, getting a group of children ready for their first Communion. She finds herself reaching for new words to help them understand the Father’s love. She tells them, “Even before you were born, you were already known and cherished by the One who calls Himself Father.” The kids stare back, eyes wide, realizing that this love is both boundless and deeply personal.
Listen to the prayers of the Mass—they keep coming back to the Father as the origin of everything good. He’s the One who sends the Son, and breathes forth the Spirit. The words might seem simple, but they carry a profound meaning: when we honor the Father, we’re honoring the very foundation of our existence.
For some, focusing on the Father feels a little unfamiliar. Maybe you’re used to thinking of God in more general terms, or you connect more easily with Jesus as friend and savior. But the Mass gently invites us to see the Father not as some distant authority, but as a living, loving presence— the source of everything that is.
And as the days go by, something shifts. People find themselves praying differently, reaching out to the Father with a new sense of closeness and trust. The words from the liturgy echo in their hearts, reminding them: you are a beloved child, called into the very life of the Trinity.
Now, this devotion to the Divine Heart of God the Father doesn’t take away from the importance of Christ or the Spirit. Instead, it reveals the unity that’s at the center of everything—a unity shaped by the overflowing love of the Father. By honoring the Father’s primacy, the Church is drawn even deeper into the mystery of divine life.
As the community continues to celebrate the Votive Mass, they discover something beautiful: the Father’s love isn’t static. It’s a living force that transforms hearts and lives. The Mass becomes a school—a place where people learn to receive and give, to forgive and to hope.
So here’s the real heart of it: the Votive Mass of the Divine Heart of God the Father isn’t just a series of prayers or rituals. It’s a path—a way for the Church to rediscover the source of all love. Through worship, reparation, and devotion, we’re invited to come closer to the Father’s heart—a heart beating with mercy, tenderness, and an unending desire to draw everyone home.
